correctness.rationale: Hilbert's degree formula specializes for length three to exactly three cases: distinct parts, one repeated part, and three equal parts. Two explicit strata bound the global gcd by a divisor of twelve, so only the primes two and three can occur. A complete parity analysis gives the exact minimum two-adic valuation in the three residue classes modulo four. For the prime three, the only way to remove the coefficient three is the equal partition, and that degree is prime to three exactly when the ambient binary degree has three-adic valuation one. Explicit strata attain each asserted minimum valuation. The bundled checker independently enumerates all length-three partitions through binary degree five hundred.

value.rationale: Length-three coincident root loci form the complete three-dimensional stratum family in the binary-form multiple-root stratification. Their projective degrees count generic complementary linear intersections. The gcd is therefore the exact universal modulus shared by all such enumerative counts at fixed binary degree. The theorem gives a complete and sharp prime-support classification, showing that the entire family has only two possible universal primes and describing exactly when each survives. This is a natural whole-family invariant rather than an arbitrary numerical slice.
